q: What was the finance P&L net profit for September 2026 as booked by event date, and how does it differ from the order-date net profit?
answer:
The finance P&L (event-date) net profit for September 2026 was a loss of ₹-1,527,829, while the order-date net profit for the same month was a loss of ₹-172,227 — the P&L (event-date) result is ₹-1,355,602 worse. This is a timing/basis gap, not a data mismatch.

- What changed (size): P&L net profit (event date) = ₹-1,527,829 vs order-date net profit = ₹-172,227 (difference ₹-1,355,602).  
- Why it matters: the two metrics use different bases — P&L net profit is booked by event/report date (captures returns/adjustments and P&L timing when they post), while net profit is measured on order date (attributes costs/revenue to the order). The catalogue definitions show P&L net profit = P&L contribution margin − P&L ad spend (event date) and net profit = contribution margin − ad spend (P&L basis) (order date).  
- Certainty / caveat: the numbers are from the certified P&L (event-date) and order-date P&L views; P&L source refresh is current as of 2026-10-14. I haven’t broken the ₹1.36M gap into lines (returns, net COGS, ad spend) yet — that would identify the dominant drivers.

Worth checking: run a P&L breakdown of P&L net profit for Sept (event date) by line (return revenue, net COGS, ad spend) to see which line(s) drive the ₹1.36M shortfall.
